content.title: About
content.content: Frog legs are the edible muscles of a frog's hind limbs, traditionally used in French, Chinese, and Southeast Asian cuisines. They have a delicate, slightly sweet flavor reminiscent of chicken and a firm yet tender texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Frog legs are considered a delicacy in France, where they are often served as "cuisses de grenouille".
In China, frog legs are commonly cooked in a soy‑ginger‑garlic sauce.
They contain more protein per gram than chicken breast while being low in fat.
Frogs are harvested during the breeding season when the muscles are at their densest.
Traditionally the legs are dusted in flour or starch before frying to create a crisp crust.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Frog legs provide about 16 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: They contain less than 2 g of fat per 100 g, most of it polyunsaturated.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Frog legs supply vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: They are a good source of iron, zinc, and phosphorus, contributing to blood health and bone strength.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: Approximately 70 kcal per 100 g, making them suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Allergy cross‑reactivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions, especially those sensitive to seafood or reptiles.

items.title: Parasitic contamination
items.content: Improperly processed legs can harbor parasites; cook thoroughly to at least 70 °C.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: High purine levels may exacerbate gout in susceptible people.

items.title: Environmental restrictions
items.content: Harvesting of wild frogs is regulated in many areas; purchase only from certified suppliers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Frog legs can be sautéed, braised, steamed, or baked. They are often marinated in wine, garlic, and herbs, then lightly coated in flour and quickly fried until golden. Serve with lemon, butter‑herb sauce, or a light vinaigrette.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh legs refrigerated at 0–2 °C in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Frozen legs retain quality for up to 3 months at –18 °C. Rinse under cold water and pat dry before cooking.
